UK ETS

UK Emissions Trading Scheme

The UK Emissions Trading Scheme puts a cap on emissions from power, heavy industry, aviation and, since 1 July 2026, domestic shipping. Each year you report your verified emissions and hand back (surrender) one allowance for every tonne. You get allowances free, buy them at auction or trade them.

Step 1

Are you in scope?

You're probably in if…

  • You run an installation burning fuel with a total rated thermal input above 20 MW, or carry out another listed activity (steel, cement, refining, chemicals, glass, paper and more)
  • You operate flights within the UK, from the UK to the EEA, or to Gibraltar and Switzerland, above the de minimis thresholds
  • You operate ships of 5,000 GT or more on UK domestic voyages, including emissions at berth in UK ports (from 1 July 2026)

You're probably out if…

  • Hospitals and small emitters on the UK ETS Authority's opt-out list for 2026–2030 follow lighter rules instead of the full scheme
  • Ultra-small emitters (under 2,500 t CO₂e a year) on the Authority's list only need to monitor their emissions
  • Waste incineration is not yet in. Its 2028 start has been delayed

Who regulates it: Environment Agency (England), SEPA (Scotland), Natural Resources Wales, NIEA (Northern Ireland), OPRED (offshore). Aviation and maritime: the regulator for your administering nation. Policy is set by the UK ETS Authority.

Step 2

Your yearly routine

  1. All yearMonitor emissions under your approved monitoring plan
  2. 28 FebFree allocation issued to eligible installations
  3. 31 MarSubmit your verified emissions report (and activity level report, if you receive free allocation)
  4. 30 AprSurrender allowances equal to last year's verified emissions

Key facts

Penalty for not surrendering
£100 per missing allowance (index-linked), and you must still surrender
First maritime report
31 March 2027, for 1 July to 31 December 2026
First maritime surrender
30 April 2028, covering both 2026 and 2027
Coming next
Greenhouse gas removals from 2029; waste incineration date to be confirmed
Practical tip

Book your verifier early. Verifiers are busiest in February and March, and new maritime operators are all chasing the same few firms for the first 31 March deadline.

Recent changes

27 August 2026

UK ETS expansion to waste incineration delayed

The government will not bring energy-from-waste into the UK ETS in 2028 as planned. A new start date is expected.
